frameworks.name: The 10-Year Million-Dollar Contract
frameworks.definition: A mental commitment device where entrepreneurs visualize a 10-year wealth accumulation goal (adding one to three zeros to net worth), then work backward to identify necessary compound decisions and investments.

claims.text: Most people overestimate what they can accomplish in one year and underestimate what they can accomplish in a decade; adding one to three zeros to net worth is achievable within ten years (Alex Hormozi, Acquisition.com).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: Major global companies that reached multi-billion valuations typically required 5-10 years from inception to that valuation milestone, demonstrating that life-changing wealth is achievable within a decade (Alex Hormozi, Acquisition.com).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: When you mentally commit to a 10-year wealth contract (accepting zero income to multiply net worth), you stop obsessing over short-term income and start making reasonable compounding bets that make winning inevitable rather than a matter of chance (Alex Hormozi, Acquisition.com).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Mental commitment to long-term wealth contract creates alignment between daily decisions and compound growth, eliminating random variance from decision-making.

claims.text: Most people choose immediate higher salary ($100k/year) over investing in self (free internship with 10x earning potential in three years) because they cannot delay gratification; this choice optimizes for present cash at the cost of future compounding (Alex Hormozi, Acquisition.com).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: career decision between immediate high pay and skill investment

claims.text: When you have limited money but abundant time and energy in early career stage, investing in self (time, experience, skills) beats investing in the stock market (S&P 500), because the asset of you compounds faster than financial assets (Alex Hormozi, Acquisition.com).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Personal skill and experience development compounds faster than market returns; the multiplier on your earning power is higher than market CAGR.
bounded_by: Does not apply to mid-career professionals with stable high income
Does not apply when financial leverage (debt, margin) can compound faster

claims.text: In early career when realizing potential earning (making money from current skills), you simultaneously forfeit investment in future potential earning; taking the short paycheck now is ripping up your million-dollar or 10x or 100x contract from a decade later (Alex Hormozi, Acquisition.com).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: early career stage, <$1M net worth, skill-dependent earning
claims.mechanism: Cash taken in year 1-3 comes from a pool of time/energy that could build 10x-100x future-earning capacity; the opportunity cost is multiplicative, not additive.

claims.text: If you know with certainty that you will 10x your net worth in ten years, you stop chasing short-term money and start making reasonable bets that compound on themselves, because winning becomes inevitable (Alex Hormozi, Acquisition.com).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

examples.text: A new employee entering Acquisition.com is offered the 10-year million-dollar contract talk: if you commit to staying and investing in yourself for a decade, accepting zero cash focus and building skills/reputation instead, you can accomplish life-changing wealth. The ask: 'Would you take a 10-year contract where you make no money for 10 years but on year 10 you add one, two, or three zeros to your net worth?' The response is almost universally yes, which Hormozi uses to say: 'Great, now act like it.'

A skilled professional is offered two paths: Path A is a job at $100k/year salary with no growth in skill/reputation. Path B is a free internship at a company willing to pay them to develop expertise, with a realistic 10x earning potential in three years, but only $35k/year during the investment period. Most people choose Path A ($100k now), forgoing the multiplicative growth of Path B, because they cannot delay gratification. After choosing Path A, they realize in year 10 they have $1M earned (3 years × $100k + 7 years degrading skill value), while Path B graduates would have $350k+ plus 10x earning optionality.

practices.text: When you have clear 10-year wealth target and mental commitment, act as if you will absolutely achieve that outcome; make compounding bets and abandon short-term income obsession.
In early career when time is abundant and capital is scarce, prioritize skill investment and experience accumulation (SME 500) over financial asset diversification (S&P 500).

Shift decision-making framework from 'how much money can I make this year' to 'what would I have to do to make it unreasonable that I don't 10x in 10 years', then execute against that long-term constraint.
